audit_notes: 1) Positivity/bounds: all 12 parameters are positive and inside their bounds; emissivities are in (0,1]; temperatures in K. 2) Adjustment: gas_conductivity raised from 0.017 to 0.023 W/m/K as an EFFECTIVE (convection-corrected) cavity conductivity. Reason: for a 16 mm argon cavity at ~24 K cavity temperature difference, Ra_w = g*beta*dT*w^3/(nu*alpha) ~ 1.5e4 (aspect ratio H/w = 75), and the EN 673 correlation Nu = 0.035*(Gr*Pr)^0.38 gives Nu ~ 1.35, so pure molecular conduction (0.017) would under-predict cavity heat transfer by ~35%; 0.017*1.35 ~ 0.023 (still within bounds). All other values unchanged. 3) Model check: the PDE uses the physical glazing thickness L = 2*t_g + w = 0.024 m for x and H = 1.2 m for y, so the y-coefficient (L/H)^2 = 4.0e-4. The x=0 / x=1 Dirichlet values are the outer/inner glass surface temperatures from the exact series-resistance solution (films + 2 panes + cavity with linearized radiation h_r = 4*sigma*T_m^3/(1/eps_c + 1/eps_g - 1)), and top/bottom are adiabatic, so the exact 2D solution is y-independent and linear in x: T(x,y) = T0 + (T1 - T0)*x. Note that the linear interior profile is a homogenized representation; physically ~0.15 K drops across each pane and ~24 K across the cavity. Closed-form reference (audited values): h_r = 0.193 W/m^2/K, k_cav,eff = 0.0261 W/m/K, R_tot = 0.791 m^2K/W, U = 1.264 W/m^2/K, q = 37.9 W/m^2, T0 (outer surface) = 264.67 K (-8.5 C), T1 (inner surface) = 288.22 K (15.1 C). Uncoated reference (eps_c = 0.84): U = 2.64 W/m^2/K, inner surface 282.88 K (9.7 C). The low-e inner surface stays well above the dew point of 20 C/50% RH room air (~282.4 K), whereas the uncoated unit is marginal. 4) Dimensionless numbers: Bi_out = h_out*R_cond = 15.5, Bi_in = h_in*R_cond = 4.78 (R_cond = glass + cavity resistance 0.621 m^2K/W), Ra_w ~ 1.5e4, Nu_cav ~ 1.35, radiation-to-conduction ratio in cavity h_r*w/k_gas ~ 0.13. 5) Simulation coefficient: overall center-of-glass U-value 1.264 W/m^2/K. 6) Solver: 2D PDE -> 'pinn', validated against the analytical linear solution above (closed-form exists, so the analytical reference is exact). 7) Stress/safety: thermal load only. Through-pane temperature drop q*t_g/k_g ~ 0.15 K -> thermal bending stress ~0.05 MPa; center-to-edge thermal stress for ~10-15 K differentials ~5-10 MPa, below the ~20-40 MPa design strength of annealed float glass; temperature range -10..20 C is well within glass, low-e coating (silver stable to >100 C when sealed) and sealant limits. Cavity pressure changes from temperature (~±5% of absolute) are within normal IGU tolerances. Audit passed. Performance gain defined as heat-loss reduction vs. the identical uncoated argon unit: 1 - 1.264/2.637 = 52.1%.
